title: User signup with email verification
description: Email-and-password signup for server apps: validated, normalized and unique emails, a NIST-style password policy, scrypt password hashing, hashed single-use 256-bit verification links, a verified-account gate, rate-limited resends that invalidate earlier links, retried idempotent verification email, enumeration-safe responses, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto (crypto.subtle, getRandomValues, randomUUID), TextEncoder/TextDecoder, btoa/atob and the Fetch Request/Response APIs.

The default scrypt hasher loads node:crypto lazily (scrypt, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual): Node.js 22+. Bun and Deno provide node:crypto but were not tested; on runtimes without it (Cloudflare Workers without nodejs_compat) inject a PasswordHasher.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlEmailSignupStore with your query executor; elsewhere implement EmailSignupStore with a unique normalized-email index and single conditional statements for createAccount, markVerified, reserveSend and consumeToken, and an atomic issueToken that inserts the new link and revokes the other pending links that are not newer.
If you already have a users table, implement EmailSignupStore against it instead of adding email_signup_accounts; keep the unique index on the normalized email.
Implement sendEmail with your email provider and pass idempotencyKey to it; set baseUrl to the absolute https URL of the page that POSTs the token to /confirm.
Pass onExistingAccount to email the owner when someone signs up with their address, and onVerified for post-verification work.

Keep the default password policy (15 to 128 code points, blocklist) or pass createPasswordPolicy({ minLength: 8 }) when passwords are only one factor of MFA; add a breached-password check for production.
Use the default scrypt hasher on Node.js 22+ or inject a PasswordHasher (Argon2id from a maintained library); verify sign-ins with the same hasher and rehash when needsRehash returns true.

Mount createEmailSignupHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins, a rateLimit(key) hook and a trusted clientIp(request); log serverError through onResult. Guard gated routes with createVerifiedGate or requireVerified.
limitations: Does not send email, sign users in or manage sessions; the application injects email delivery and reads the session for the verified gate.

Responses are identical for new and registered emails, but latency differs: a new account also inserts a token and sends the email. Queue the email (sendEmail resolving after enqueue) if timing matters.

An attacker can register an unverified account for someone else's address first; the owner is told through onExistingAccount when they sign up, but recovering the account needs a password reset flow (see password-reset). Delete long-unverified accounts on a schedule.
Send retries are immediate in-process attempts with short waits; durable retries across restarts need a queue (see email-outbox). A failed delivery still uses one resend slot.
Email normalization lowercases the whole address and does not fold provider aliases (plus tags, Gmail dots); internationalized (non-ASCII) addresses are rejected.
The default policy's blocklist is small; it is not a breached-password check.
scrypt at the default cost (N = 2^17, r = 8) uses about 128 MiB per hash on the libuv thread pool; rate-limit signups and size the server accordingly.
Rate limiting of the HTTP routes is a hook only; back it with the rate-limit module or your gateway. Per-account resend limits are enforced by the store.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under real multi-connection contention.
Production database correctness, email deliverability, hashing cost tuning and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: routes: POST {prefix}/signup and /resend → 202 {ok:true} for every outcome; POST {prefix}/confirm → 200
a registered email gets the same 202, never 409; the owner is told through onExistingAccount
password 15-128 chars, no composition rules; scrypt N=2^17; 400 weak-password with problems
token stored as SHA-256 hash; 24 h default ttl, single use; confirm is a POST, not a GET link

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/email-signup.test.mjs tests/email-signup-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: emails are trimmed, lowercased and validated (WHATWG syntax, dotted domain, length limits) before storage and comparison
four concurrent signups with the same normalized email create exactly one account (memory store and PGlite unique index)
the default password policy enforces 15 to 128 code points, a common-password and email blocklist and no composition rules; an injected policy replaces it
the default scrypt hasher writes $scrypt$ln=17,r=8,p=1 PHC strings with a 16-byte random salt, verifies with timingSafeEqual, refuses absurd stored parameters and reports needsRehash
the link carries a 256-bit base64url token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored; it expires after 24 hours and works once
unverified accounts are refused by requireVerified, assertVerified and the HTTP gate (403 email-unverified, 401 signed out) until confirmed
exactly one of four concurrent confirms verifies the account and onVerified runs once (memory store and PGlite)

resends are limited by a cooldown and a per-window cap on an injected clock, concurrent resends cannot exceed them, each resend revokes earlier links, and interleaved concurrent resends always leave at least one working link (memory store and PGlite)
every verification email carries an idempotency key per token; retries reuse it; final failure revokes the link and is reported only in serverError

signup with a registered email returns the same public result, creates nothing, keeps the existing password and calls onExistingAccount; a throwing onExistingAccount is reported only in serverError, so the HTTP response stays the same 202 as a new email with a failed send
a link stops working when the account email changes after it was sent

HTTP adapter: 202 identical bodies for signup and resend, 400 invalid-email, weak-password with problems and invalid-token, 200 confirm, origin check, 429 from rateLimit keyed by IP and email, bounded body, cache-control no-store and referrer-policy no-referrer
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: core, NIST-style policy, scrypt hasher, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter with a verified gate.
